title: "No More, on Earth No More
description: "No More, on Earth No More in Tonic Solfa to FRANCONIA, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: William Gaskell wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 352, “No More!”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to FRANCONIA; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: "No more, on earth no more, Shall beam for us that eye; Closed in a strange for-get-ful-ness For-ev-er it must lie.

lines: Shall beam for us that eye;
Within the mournful halls of death
Shall those dear lips be heard;
Cold silence there hath fixed its seal,
But Faith stands forth, she points on high,
That eye is dim with tears;
But bright, and brighter still, the scene
But looks of light, born of a bliss
That voice is faint with pain;
To look through as its own."

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Gaskell died in 1884.
credits: Words by William Gaskell (1805–1884), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to FRANCONIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
